Hi Paul,

Thanks for the photo, that tells me what I needed. I can see both NerdQaxe++ boards on their printed bases, each with the big heatsink fan fitted, and the second fan (the small Snowman one) sitting loose on the base next to the board. The screen on the right hand unit reads BM1370, about 4.75 TH/s, ASIC at 55 C and the main fan at roughly 4200 rpm, so the miners themselves are healthy and hashing normally. The only thing missing is the screw set for that second fan.

That second fan is the rear fan. Its job is to pull heat away from the voltage regulator area and off the back of the board, so it helps stability and longevity, but it is not required for the unit to run safely. At 55 C on the ASICs you are in a good place right now. Two things worth doing in the meantime: make sure the loose fan is actually plugged into its header and spinning (you should feel air moving), and leave it sitting where it is on the base blowing across the board rather than standing it on its side, since that is roughly the position it mounts in anyway.

On the hardware itself, it mounts with four standard fan screws that self tap straight into the printed base, no nuts needed. For a 25mm thick fan that means screws about 30 to 35mm long, M3 coarse or the usual black self tapping fan screws that come in any 120mm fan box. If you happen to have a spare PC case fan lying around, its screws will do the job today. Otherwise I have passed this to the team so they can get the correct screw set for both units out to you, and a colleague is picking it up today and will confirm by email.

If you want a hand with anything else on these, pool setup, tuning or noise, our Discord is very active at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD, our hardware lead, is there as @nullhashrate.

Best, Hal
